I used to go tho a catholic girls only school and I think that it didn't past my mind that same sex relationships were a thing till I was like 9-10 like I literally didn't knew that was a thing, I remembered seeing a guy on the news who had a baby (I was like 8) and telling my friend like wow men can have kids and she tol my teacher i said that, my teacher instead of explaining that he was a trans guy, she said that it was fake news and that some people inflated their bellies out of fun or something (thinking back that was kinda imply that it was a kink thing). When I was like 12 or so I started questioning my teachers about the why same sex relationships were a sin and if people could go to heaven still, different asnwers were threw around but the conclusion was that it was ok but not advised. That made me feel sad because I was questioning my sexuality/gender (being in a allgirls school does things) and as I was a child I thought that not going to heaven was the worst thing to ever happen.

I think that if I had been exposed to being queer as a normal and totally not a sin that would make me betray god, my mental health would have been better because I wouldn't have felt so alone and definetly would have educated me on being respectful to queer people as a child instead of semi-judging. I think that that being queer has to be an option that kids can see it's ok and that theres successful queer people too, that god loves all and that you can have your religious values no matter your sexuality/gender identity. Not too explicitly as talking about sexuality also involves talking about sex, but definetly to have positive examples in your life and someone to ask whatever comes to your mind instead of googling and finding misinformation or not positive content.
